text:
julia-customer: hey team, we started getting a ton of 429s this morning around 07:12 UTC, ~80% of requests failing, our users in EU hit timeouts. nothing changed on our app side that we know of. any quick checks?

sara-support: hi Julia :wave: can you share a few request ids or sample timestamps? also which API key/client id?

julia-customer: sure — client id acct-AZ12, sample x-request-ids: rq_01F3, rq_01F4, rq_01F7. we see `RateLimit-Remaining: 0` in the response and `Retry-After: 2`.

sara-support: thanks — i'm pulling logs now. mike are you able to look at ingress throttle metrics for acct-AZ12?

mike-sre: looking. dashboard shows a sharp RPM spike starting 07:10 UTC from one /24. TPM also climbed. interestingly, requests are coming in with many different API keys but same source IP (X-Forwarded-For shows 52.64.12.33).

dan-engineering: 52.64.12.33 rings a bell — that's the IP of a regional CDN / reverse-proxy we onboarded last week (proxy-shim v2). deploy-bot: deploy proxy-shim v2 to edge eu-west at 05:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: :information_source: deploy completed: proxy-shim v2 @ 05:00 UTC (sha: a1b2c3).

ethan-infra: here's a quick grep of logs (07:09-07:20):
```
# tail -n 200 access.log | grep 'acct-AZ12' | sed -n '1,50p'
2026-02-10T07:09:58Z 52.64.12.33 acct-AZ12 POST /v1/generate 200 x-req:rq_01E9
2026-02-10T07:10:03Z 52.64.12.33 acct-AZ12 POST /v1/generate 429 x-req:rq_01F3
2026-02-10T07:10:03Z 52.64.12.33 acct-AZ12 POST /v1/generate 429 x-req:rq_01F4
2026-02-10T07:10:05Z 52.64.12.33 acct-AZ12 POST /v1/generate 429 x-req:rq_01F7
# pattern: burst of retries inside 1-2s windows
```

sara-support: so the pattern looks like a burst coming from the proxy. could be client retries being collapsed and replayed by proxy. are headers like `X-Request-Id` preserved?

mike-sre: not always. i see the proxy reusing connections and replaying queued requests which defeats our per-key smoothing. also many of these requests carry different API keys (customers using same aggregated proxy). that means our per-key RPM limits are being hit because upstream is multiplexing.

julia-customer: our app uses per-device keys rotated every hour (we issue short-lived tokens). we use exponential backoff but backoff jitter was not implemented — it was a deterministic retry at 1s, 2s, 4s. could that cause sync?

dan-engineering: yes deterministic backoff + proxy connection pooling = synchronized spikes. plus our gateway's `x-forwarded-for` shows the proxy IP, so at our edge we attribute all requests to one origin and can't do per-client shaping correctly.

sara-support: immediate mitigations: 1) temporary per-account RPM bump for acct-AZ12 while we triage, 2) ask CDN partner to disable request replaying/connection re-use for this client, 3) advise Julia to add jitter to retry logic. any other quick wins?

mike-sre: we can enable `RateLimit-By-Api-Key` enforcement that uses auth header instead of source IP (experimental flag). i'll flip it for support-mode if you approve. it'll reduce cross-customer impact but might bypass some aggregated safeguards.

julia-customer: yes please enable. urgent customer-facing error rates are high, we need a short window to stabilize. happy to accept short-term quota bump.

ethan-infra: done — temporarily raised RPM quota for acct-AZ12 by 3x (expires in 2 hours). added a note to the incident log.

sara-support: mike, can you capture traces showing retry loops? a snippet of `curl -I` to reproduce header behavior would help.

mike-sre: here's a minimal repro against the proxy vs direct. proxy path: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://proxy.example.cdn/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}\n"
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
RateLimit-Limit: 120
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 1
X-Proxy-Request-Id: pxy_abbc
```

direct path (bypassing CDN):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}\n"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
RateLimit-Limit: 120
RateLimit-Remaining: 118
```

dan-engineering: that confirms the proxy is showing different semantics. action items: - rollback proxy-shim v2 config for edge eu-west to previous connection-handling mode OR ask CDN to stop request coalescing; - ship a small client-side guidance doc for jittered exponential backoff and token rotation best-practices; - enable `RateLimit-By-Api-Key` experimental flag for 1 hour; - add a temporary alert threshold in console for cross-key spikes from same source IP.

mike-sre: i'm rolling the experimental flag now. monitor shows successful reduction in 429s for acct-AZ12 within 30s.

julia-customer: after the bump + flag toggle, errors dropped from 82% -> 6% within 3 minutes. huge improvement, thank you. we'll push a client patch to add jitter tonight.

sara-support: great — follow-up: we'll keep the quota bump for 2 hours as planned, engineering will engage the CDN partner for a config rollback and client guidance will be drafted. can you confirm when you deploy jittered retries and token behaviour so we can close the thread? :thumbsup:

julia-customer: planning deploy by 20:00 UTC, i'll post an update when done. thanks for the quick turnaround.

mike-sre: adding notes to postmortem: root cause = proxy replay + deterministic client retries + token churn causing many valid keys to be multiplexed through single IP; mitigation = per-api-key rate-limiting, CDN config revert, client jitter + small quota increase.

ethan-infra: incident closed-ish — monitoring will auto-close after 48h stable. marking for follow-up with partnerships team to change onboarding checklist for any new proxy: require `preserve-x-request-id` and non-replay connection policy.

sara-support: thanks everyone. marking this resolved in support queue pending Julia's confirm.

julia-customer: confirmed deployment at 20:12 UTC, 429s stayed <2% after patch. closing from our side. :lock:
